subject: Trial plan + competitive gaps after today's bakeoff
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Trial plan + competitive gaps after today's bakeoff

Hi Samir / Claire —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to act from. I focused this around the two things you emphasized: predictable latency at 95th percentile for short queries (~150 token prompts) and clear isolation/telemetry for auditability.

Summary of pain & goals we heard
- Latency: 95th pctl target <= 150ms for interactive ticket triage flows.
- Cost predictability: unit economics need to be stable across spikes for at-scale analysis jobs.
- Compliance: request-level audit logs + KMS integration for payloads.
- Competitive gaps: OrbitAI's token pricing looks cheaper but they lack per-request KV caching and their telemetry is noisy.

Immediate proposal (what we can deliver in the next 2 weeks)
1) 48-hour trial window on a dedicated pool configured to mirror your traffic profile (we'll load a 30-minute trace you provide).
2) Two targeted tests we'll run from your environment and ours:
   - Latency sweep: 10k synthetic short prompts at steady qps to surface 95th pctl.
   - Isolation/telemetry check: sample 500 requests with sensitive fields to validate KMS/HSM and audit log records.
3) Competitive comparison sheet: we've attached a vendor matrix showing gaps and test vectors we recommend for apples-to-apples comparison.

Open questions we flagged on the call (please confirm):
- Can you share the 30-minute production trace (anonymized) we discussed? Prefer JSON traces with timestamps.
- Are there any additional redline items in your security questionnaire beyond SOC2 and KMS?

Next steps / owners
- Samir / Claire: share trace + confirm trial window availability (we suggested Tue 2/23 start).
- Monica: prepare trial pool + test harness; ship trial-config.yaml and vendor matrix by EOD Monday.
- Rishi: validate the audit-log schema and KMS onboarding checklist.
- Vanessa: lead the performance sweep and post-test analysis.

Attachments: redwood-competitive-matrix.xlsx, trial-config.yaml, mutual-action-plan.pdf

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff once you confirm the 2/23 date.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@healthgrid.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-02-14T17:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan + competitive gaps after today's bakeoff

Thanks Monica — clear and helpful. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Trace: we can provide a redacted 30-minute trace (no PHI), ETA Fri 2/19. Format will be a gzipped JSON. Will that work?
2) Trial window: 2/23 is OK but we need the ability to run one of the latency sweeps from our east-coast region to ensure cross-region behavior is covered. Can you confirm that?
3) Competitor note: OrbitAI also advertised runtime quantization which they claim reduces cost by ~30% for our workloads — can your latency sweep include an equivalent quantized run so we can compare both cost and 95th pctl?

Also looping in Claire for procurement timing on the trial (she may need a short MSA amendment).

Date: 2027-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan + competitive gaps after today's bakeoff — confirmations

Samir —

Yes on all counts. Quick answers and confirmations: 
- Trace format: gzipped JSON is perfect. Please upload to the Drive link in the related_links list (or reply with a signed upload link).
- Cross-region runs: we will run the latency sweep from both us-west-2 (our default trial pool) and us-east-1 (your request) — results will be split by region in the final report.
- Quantized run: we can include an equivalent run with our 8-bit quantized profile so you can compare cost vs 95th pctl. That will be a separate test in the matrix.

I attached the trial-config.yaml with the exact pool sizing and test vectors. For procurement / MSA: happy to provide a short amendment and a trial addendum; Vanessa, can you confirm whether we need legal to prepare the amendment or if a simple signature from Claire is sufficient?

Proposed timeline (2-week look):
- 2/19: HealthGrid uploads trace + Claire confirms procurement path.
- 2/22: Redwood prepares trial pool + pre-run smoke tests.
- 2/23–2/24: Trial window (latency sweeps + telemetry sampling).
- 2/26: Detailed results and runbook delivered; sync to review.

If this looks good I'll send the calendar invite for the 2/23 kickoff and tag the run owners.

—Monica

Date: 2027-02-16T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: HealthGrid trial — owners and checklist (please ACK)

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the plan. This is an internal ownership assignment so we can move fast once HealthGrid uploads the trace. Please reply with ACK and any blockers.

Owners / asks
- Vanessa: ownership of the latency sweep (us-west-2 + us-east-1). Deliverable: latency report + csv of raw timings. Target: run completed 2/23 end of day. Attachment: trial-config.yaml.
- Rishi: security checklist and audit-log validation. Deliverable: conformance doc that maps HealthGrid questionnaire items to our audit schema. Target: 2/22 COB.
- Aditya: trial infra provisioning and canary pre-runs (smoke test). Deliverable: pool IPs, firewall rules, and canary logs. Target: 2/22 EOD.
- Monica: overall project owner + post-trial readout.

Known risks / mitigations
- If HealthGrid's trace shows sustained bursts >10x baseline, we will throttle to the agreed steady-state qps for the latency sweep and capture burst behavior separately.
- If procurement needs legal amendments, ask Claire for a redline window and we'll coordinate with legal.

Please ACK and I'll drop a short Loom with the test-run steps.

—Monica
